title: Move the shell's sub-14px inline font sizes onto the lab type tokens
body:
## Summary
26 inline fontSize values below the lab's 14px type floor remain across five shell files (CatalogMatrix, MatrixBatchDrain, CanonView, CatalogTree, StepCrashBoundary).

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/lab-tokens.css:10 declares the lab type scale with a '>=14px floor' (--lab-fs-xs: 14px), and LayoutLab/PipelineRail/ActivityChip/StepCrashBoundary already read var(--lab-fs-*). The matrix, drain, canon and tree surfaces still hard-code 11-13px: src/components/layout-lab/CatalogMatrix.tsx:141,162,194,211,247 (12-13px), src/components/layout-lab/MatrixBatchDrain.tsx:85,106,120,147,158,171,206 (12px), src/components/layout-lab/CanonView.tsx:28-30,124,129,153 (12-13px), src/components/layout-lab/CatalogTree.tsx:173,183,239,252,265 (11-12px; :239 trips the repo's own 12px eslint floor warning), src/components/layout-lab/StepCrashBoundary.tsx:148 (13px). Fixed = each site reads a --lab-fs-* token (or ui/MicroLabel for justified dense meta), with a source-scan ratchet so the count only shrinks. Distinct from the coach-and-guidance token card, which covers the banner/digest files.

## Flow
- open /layout -> Matrix: column legend, header labels, drain notes and progress lines render at 12-13px
- Canon: scope chips, Edit/Delete, category heads at 12-13px
- build order: add a comment-stripped source-scan test counting fontSize < 14 over this context's files (seed red at 26), migrate file by file to var(--lab-fs-xs/sm), ratchet to 0

## Expected impact
Operators reading the Matrix and Canon get the lab's declared floor; dense surfaces (matrix header, drain summary) may wrap differently.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - shell text meets the lab's declared 14px floor
Before: 26 inline sub-14px fontSize sites in 5 of the context's 18 files; 0 --lab-fs tokens in CanonView, CatalogMatrix, MatrixBatchDrain
After: 0 sub-14px sites; ratchet test green
Method: simulation - counted by grep over the tree; the visual effect on the dense matrix header needs a render check the round did not run
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -oE "fontSize: 1[0-3]\b" per file: CanonView 6, CatalogMatrix 6, CatalogTree 5, MatrixBatchDrain 8, StepCrashBoundary 1 (total 26); grep var(--lab-fs: CanonView 0, CatalogMatrix 0, MatrixBatchDrain 0. src/components/layout-lab/lab-tokens.css:10 '--lab-fs-xs: 14px' under 'type scale (>=14px floor)'
instrument: source-scan vitest over the context's file_paths (comments stripped) counting inline fontSize < 14; seeded red at 26, ratchet shrink-only

title: Give the header popovers focus entry and restore like the dialogs they declare
body:
## Summary
The ActivityChip and Bridge Doctor popovers declare role=dialog but never move focus in or restore it, and each hand-rolls the same outside-click + document-Escape effect.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/ActivityChip.tsx:46-58 and src/components/layout-lab/LabBridgeStrip.tsx:62-74 carry the same useEffect (mousedown outside -> close, document keydown Escape -> close); both render role=dialog (ActivityChip.tsx:83, LabBridgeStrip.tsx:112). Neither focuses into the panel on open nor returns focus to the trigger on Escape, so a keyboard user opening 'What is running' or 'Bridge Doctor' stays on the trigger and must Tab blindly; and the document-level Escape also fires while another dialog (LabSearch's Modal) owns the key, closing both. Fixed = one shared popover hook (open/close, outside click, Escape scoped to the popover, focus first control on open, restore on close), used by both sites.

## Flow
- focus the activity chip, press Enter -> panel opens, focus stays on the chip
- press Escape -> panel closes; focus was never inside it
- open LabSearch (Ctrl+K) with a popover open, press Escape -> both close
- build order: write the keyboard test for both popovers (seed red), extract the hook into layout-lab/hooks (sibling lab-hooks context owns that folder), migrate both

## Expected impact
Keyboard and AT users can enter and leave both header popovers; risk is the hook landing in a sibling-owned folder.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - header popovers are keyboard-operable dialogs
Before: focus moves into the popover on open in 0 of 2; focus restores to the trigger on Escape in 0 of 2; 2 duplicated close effects
After: 2 of 2 and 2 of 2; 1 shared hook
Method: simulation - read both effects; no keyboard test exists to take the figure
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/layout-lab/ActivityChip.tsx:51 const onKey = (e) => { if (e.key === 'Escape') setOpen(false); }; src/components/layout-lab/LabBridgeStrip.tsx:67 const handleKey = (e) => { if (e.key === 'Escape') setOpen(false); }; neither file calls .focus()
instrument: vitest: open each popover via keyboard, assert document.activeElement is inside role=dialog, Escape returns focus to the trigger; seeded red 0/2

title: Stop the lab search shortcut opening on top of another modal dialog
body:
## Summary
Ctrl/Cmd+K and '/' open lab search from a window listener with no check for an already-open aria-modal dialog, so search stacks over the narrow-shell drawer or a ConfirmDialog.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/LabSearch.tsx:189-206 (useLabSearchShortcut) opens on any Ctrl/Cmd+K, and on '/' outside a text field. The narrow-shell LabDrawer (aria-modal, focus-trapped) and the canon delete ConfirmDialog are both aria-modal; with either open, the shortcut mounts a second modal over it, and two focus traps then compete. Fixed = the shortcut does nothing while an [aria-modal=true] other than the search itself is open (or the decision is to close the underlying one first).

## Flow
- narrow viewport -> open the Catalogs drawer -> press Ctrl+K -> search modal opens over the drawer
- Canon -> Delete -> ConfirmDialog open -> press '/' -> search opens over the confirm
- build order: test with an open aria-modal + both shortcuts (seed red), guard the listener

## Expected impact
Keyboard users stop landing in stacked modals; risk: an operator who relies on Ctrl+K from inside the drawer has to press Escape first (which now works, a608771e).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one modal at a time
Before: shortcut opens search over an open aria-modal for 2 of 2 shortcuts (by reading the listener)
After: 0 of 2
Method: simulation - listener read; not reproduced in a test this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/layout-lab/LabSearch.tsx:195-200 if ((e.key === 'k' || e.key === 'K') && (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey)) { e.preventDefault(); setOpen(true); } else if (e.key === '/' && !typing ...) { ...setOpen(true); } - no aria-modal check
instrument: vitest renderHook(useLabSearchShortcut) with a mounted <div role=dialog aria-modal=true>, dispatch Ctrl+K and '/', assert open stays false; seeded red 2/2

title: Announce or focus the new view when the header switches Catalogs/Matrix/Canon/Game
body:
## Summary
Switching the lab view swaps the canvas in shell state with no focus move and no announcement, so a screen-reader user hears nothing change.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/LayoutLab.tsx:134-137 call nav.view(...) and the AnimatePresence block swaps the canvas; the location lives in state, not a route change, so no framework route announcer fires, and the document title (useDynamicTitle via ActivityChip) reflects activity, not the view. The app-shell golden path's accessibility posture: 'Navigation moves focus... where the switch is not a route change, announce it yourself.' Fixed = after a view switch, a polite live region names the view (or focus moves to the new view wrapper, now id=lab-view tabIndex=-1 since c0b2d54b).

## Flow
- focus the Matrix header button, press Enter -> the matrix renders, AT reads only 'Matrix, pressed'
- build order: test that a view click yields a live-region text naming the view (seed red 0/4), add the region in LayoutLab

## Expected impact
AT users get confirmation of each view switch; moving focus would pull keyboard users off the header row, so an announcement is the gentler option.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - view switches are stated, not only painted
Before: 0 of 4 view switches announce the new view or move focus into it
After: 4 of 4
Method: simulation - render read; the instrument is a short test
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/layout-lab/LayoutLab.tsx:134-137 <Button active={view === 'matrix'} onClick={() => nav.view('matrix')}> ...; grep 'aria-live' / '.focus(' in LayoutLab.tsx -> 0
instrument: vitest: render LayoutLab, click each view button, assert a role=status region's text names the view; seeded red 0/4
